function.mechanism: Dissolved CO2 carbonates and acidifies foods/beverages; gaseous CO2 displaces oxygen in headspace and can limit aerobic spoilage; solid CO2 (dry ice) cools via sublimation.

adi.basis: EFSA (2019) concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Carbon dioxide (E290) was considered not of safety concern at reported uses; no numerical ADI considered necessary.

adi.basis: JECFA entry states ADI NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Some carbonated waters and carbonated beverages can have low pH, which may contribute to dental erosion risk in susceptible consumers; this is formulation/context dependent and not a strong intrinsic toxicity signal for CO2 itself.
A 2024 systematic review reported uncertainty about whether hypertensive patients should avoid sparkling water; evidence remains inconclusive.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2019): no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses.
JECFA: ADI not specified for carbon dioxide.
Randomized human study found no effect of carbonation on glycemic response or gastric emptying (PMID:28606564).

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI set by EFSA or JECFA, so standard ADI exceedance calculations are not applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus indicates low concern (EFSA no numerical ADI/no safety concern, JECFA ADI not specified, FDA GRAS under cGMP), and CO2 is endogenous and physiologically regulated; available human data do not show a convincing additive-specific toxicity signal.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 re-evaluation: no numerical ADI needed
No IARC classification identified for carbon dioxide
Only weak, context-dependent concerns from beverage matrix/pH studies
